troponin I, caldesmon and tropomyosin are able to immobilize the actin filament in the presence of the myosin head.
the binding of troponin and caldesmon to actin filaments restricts the structural alterations in actin occurring on binding of the myosin head.
troponin I (TnI) and caldesmon, two thin‐filament proteins, restrict structural alterations occurring on binding of skeletal myosin subfragments to the actin filament.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the regulatory proteins on the structural and mechanical properties of the actomyosin complex.
the role of troponin and caldesmon in regulating the structure of actin filments and in the mechanism of contraction of skeletal muscle.
the role of troponin‐tropomyosin and caldesmon in the regulation of actin structure and the interaction of the actin‐containing filament with the myosin head.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the troponin‐tropomyosin system and caldesmon act synergistically on the actin filament, and that the effect is potentiated by myosin subfragments.
the effect of troponic proteins on myosin binding is due to the inhibition of structural changes in actin.
troponin I is an inhibitor of myosin ATPase activity, whereas caldesmon is an inhibitor of the actomyosin ATPase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
troponin I, caldesmon and tropomyosin are all involved in maintaining the actin structure, and the cooperative action of these three proteins is required for the maintenance of the actin structure.

troponin and caldesmon, which are both present in the thin filament, are capable of restricting actin‐myosin interactions.
